q: How do we prove the CO2 saving from replacing high-bay lights with LEDs?
title: High-bay LED retrofit saving
short: Count fittings and wattage before and after, multiply by operating hours to get kWh, then use 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25. Back it with the purchase invoice, a photo log, and electricity bills or a sub-meter reading for the lighting circuit. Lenders and verifiers trust measured kWh over nameplate maths.

ul: Old and new fitting counts and wattage, with the supplier invoice.
Operating hours per day and days per year.
A month of sub-meter readings before and after, if you can fit one.
Using rated watts of the old lamps without driver losses.
Ignoring hours cut by daylight or sensors, which add to the saving.
Claiming the saving before the new lights run for a full month.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
